scope: 225 source records reviewed/proposed; only 42 integrated SEL positions remain pending cross-strand application qualification.
meaning: Original untested task design, not a child-performance study, clinical prescription, fitness ranking or learner-state update.

protocols.task: On a clear floor route, choose stable shapes on different appropriate bases and at low/middle/higher accessible levels. Perform two still positions and a controlled transfer between them, then vary speed or route and recover a deliberately small self-initiated change. Repeat with an appropriate lightweight object and in relation to a partner: coordinate side-by-side shapes or mirror a change without unsafe supporting/lifting. Older source rows retain smooth transfers in relation to another person and equipment; a single held pose is insufficient.
protocols.positive: The learner maintains or recovers intended body control and shows a useful adjustment, not only labels balance.
protocols.nearMiss: One frozen position, unsafe partner loading or an adult holding the learner in place does not establish the whole operation.
protocols.transfer: Change the base, safe route or partner position and demonstrate a controlled adjustment.
protocols.sourceConditions: Preserve each exact source row’s body/shape/level, equipment, partner and transfer duties. The unrelated NCERT60-second posture is not imported as an Ontario norm.

protocols.task: Use a marked clear route to walk/run, hop, skip, jump and land, then respond to direction, stop and speed cues. Combine patterns at different levels and pathways with/without a lightweight object and with a partner at a safe distance. Grade1 separately demonstrates stopping near people/equipment. Grade2 includes actual one- and two-foot take-offs; Grade3 chooses height or distance and demonstrates both take-off types. Grade4 includes an actual appropriately low supported take-off height and controlled landing with a prepared adult/surface; no fixed bench height or distance score. Grade5 changes body actions for a controlled height/distance jump. Grade6 combines varied routes, speeds and others/equipment.
protocols.positive: Recognisably different movement patterns remain controlled through the source-specific combination or landing condition.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming movements, one successful unplanned jump or merely walking the route cannot certify the whole canonical pattern inventory.
protocols.transfer: Change the path/cue order or object arrangement and retain control.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual safe capability/access and adult-prepared environment retained; wheelchair/adapted source participation is not falsely recorded as mastery of every canonical walk/run/hop pattern.

protocols.task: Use a soft ball, beanbag and light disc or similarly appropriate shapes. Deliberately send by hand and foot at changed safe levels/directions/distances, receive a changed incoming path and control arrival. Older rows include an appropriate hand/implement strike and a receiving aid, with actual speed/force adjustment and an explained/demonstrated movement principle such as following the intended direction or absorbing arrival. Keep a foot-stop/other body receiving case as an explicit source task where required; a hand catch alone never proves that case.
protocols.positive: Intentional release/contact, safe body positioning and adjusted controlled arrival are actually demonstrated across the selected source variety.
protocols.nearMiss: Accidental contact, one unadjusted throw or only identifying an equipment picture is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Move the target/partner or change the supplied object’s path, speed or equipment and adapt.
protocols.sourceConditions: No universal distance, dominance or athletic norm. The whole existing hand-catching and throwing checks remain separate from a source-specific foot/equipment condition.

protocols.task: Secure a suitable object, then retain control while moving through a clear changing route. Use more than one object size/shape and holding arrangement: hands, forearm/body support and an appropriate scoop or similar aid. Change speed, path and relation to another person/obstacle. For Grade6 use a no-contact modified keep-away or route-change situation with clear boundaries, maintaining possession while choosing a new path. Controlled carrying is a valid source implementation; continuous dribbling is an illustrative option, not an invented universal duty. If selected, actual foot/stick dribbling must be demonstrated rather than inferred from hand catching.
protocols.positive: The object remains deliberately controlled through the required movement changes, not merely caught once at the beginning.
protocols.nearMiss: An isolated catch, walking without the object, repeatedly dropping it or a static posed photo is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Change object, support/aid, route and other-person position and adapt the retention.
protocols.sourceConditions: Whole Catching includes secure retention during modest travel; combine with actual locomotor control and the precise source conditions, without silently redefining either old claim.

protocols.task: Actually play more than one individual and small-group activity from the original game set. Identify its goal, space/boundaries, allowed movement/equipment, relevant roles and agreed safety/fair-play rules. Explain two rules and what would happen without them, then apply them consistently. Share an idea, respond to another participant and complete an agreed fair role. Take turns and listen; an adult’s repeated reminders or the group result alone do not prove an individual whole claim.
protocols.positive: The learner connects an actual game component to how the activity works and participates accordingly.
protocols.nearMiss: Reciting a rule word or describing only the equipment without applying the activity’s components is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Play a changed version with a different boundary, role or allowed action and explain/apply the new structure.
protocols.sourceConditions: No winner/fitness/positive mood criterion. Group-work, rules vocabulary and their actual hard-chain checks remain; the source is not reduced to an English word quiz.

protocols.task: After actually playing examples from different activity families, sort the original activity cards by the supplied functional model: accuracy at a target; return across a divided area; striking then retrieving to limit runs; retaining/advancing possession against opposition; individual non-opposition task. Explain a common feature and an effective observed tactic for the chosen families. Count the cards in each group, compare totals and order the categories by count to retain the complete existing classification/count operation; that extra whole-card check is not a new HPE numeric requirement.
protocols.positive: Classification follows the actual rules/objective/interaction, not colour of equipment or country/name; reasoning is tied to actual participation.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming five labels, sorting by ball colour or claiming that all activities use one universal taxonomy is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Classify a changed original game from its declared rules and justify it; a game may require stating the chosen dominant structure when features overlap.
protocols.sourceConditions: The official source calls its chart one possible model. No new five-category mastery topic or compulsory team-sport preference.

protocols.task: In an actual modified game, pause or use an agreed decision break to identify two plausible actions and a likely consequence of each under the current objective, rules, space and other-player positions. Choose with a reason, perform the action, inspect the result and make a fresh decision when the situation changes. For younger rows use changed target distance or a clear versus blocked route. Older rows use an unmarked receiver, placing a return away from an opponent, positioning to retrieve, or protecting possession without contact. Do not interpret “stop” as a demand to freeze bodily movement before every live action.
protocols.positive: A reasoned choice is physically applied and adapted to a changed game situation; fluent motor execution alone does not prove the decision criterion.
protocols.nearMiss: An accurate pass to a covered option, a memorised tactic name, a discussion without action or a lucky point alone is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Change the target, defender position or activity family, identify the new options/consequences and actually apply a suitable choice.
protocols.sourceConditions: Whole Stop, Think, Then Choose is domain-general and its consequence prerequisite remains. No sport-specific decision clone, automatic design/study-strategy transfer or new hard dependency is inferred.

protocols.task: Implement a varied rotation of individual and small-group physical activities across days: a comfortable travel/route activity, an object game, a movement-to-music activity and a cooperative task. Record actual participation according to capabilities and the activity-specific access arrangements. Observe knowing the task, readiness, respectful communication, fair contribution and response to others; a passive worksheet is not participation. Use the actual games and movement tasks already specified in the movement programme.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: For group-work contribution retain own idea, response to another idea and completion of a fair part. For rules retain reasons for two relevant agreements, consistent following and a reasoned no-rule contrast. Keep these checks separate from a general impression of compliance or enthusiasm.

protocols.task: After actual participation in several individual and group activities, identify and compare factors affecting the learner’s own experience. Use an activity-choice card and before/after access adjustment: for example a more accessible play area, a manageable group size or a meaningful choice of role. Explain what helped, what did not and a possible change. No requirement to like every activity or to disclose culture, disability, family circumstances or private feelings.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The self-knowledge contribution is about preferences and strengths, not a claim that liking PE establishes all identity knowledge. Retain the broader existing All about me checks with safely chosen important people/helpers and similarities/differences, without forced private disclosure.

protocols.task: Use an actual school-day map and supplied local home/community opportunity cards: a safe walk/wheel route, free movement space, an indoor alternative and a paid/distant option. Identify realistic daily opportunities and reasons. Older panels compare cost, travel, time, access, peer/cultural relevance and preferences, then propose a feasible response to an obstacle rather than blame the child or family. Test a changed case such as a closed outdoor space or unavailable transport.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: For the routine contribution retain a real chosen routine, when/how plan, week record, reflection and one way to support someone else. For a decision contribution compare at least two feasible options and likely consequences before choosing; naming a barrier alone is not a solution.

protocols.task: Provide the source-required daily minimum 20-minute physical-activity opportunity with appropriate gradual warm-up and cool-down, moderate-to-vigorous participation to the best of each learner’s ability and actual access/support. Prepare a safe adult-supervised circuit from movement tasks, movement-to-music, travel and modified games. Record date, actual activity, duration, preparation, recovery and access/support; do not count an invented example log as a learner’s participation. A gentle cool-down is explicitly taught and performed, not inferred from doing the warm-up.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Preserve the complete preparation claim: follow or choose a suitable gradual sequence, controlled comfortable mobility, a relevant preparation reason communicated by demonstration/picture/explanation, and adjustment for discomfort. Leadership, maximal exertion and pain tolerance are not criteria.

protocols.task: Compare safe activity cases and explain practical physical and mental/brain-health benefits using the grade panel: physical examples include sustained activity, muscular work or easier comfortable movement; mental examples include attention and memory support or reduced risk of depression. Use population-level possibilities, not a promise that a session makes every child happy or cures distress. Younger panels use concrete attention, energy and enjoyable social participation cases; do not require diagnosis or detailed organ physiology.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The Basic Body Needs link contributes exercise/heart/muscle and body-needs reasoning. Retain its full food-energy, water-hydration, sleep-rest/growth and exercise checks separately. It does not alone certify the mental-health part; the explicit cases and explanations supply that source duty. Do not add advanced physiology or harmful-substance knowledge as a new prerequisite for explaining an everyday benefit.

concreteCases.reason: Repeated appropriate participation can develop cardiorespiratory capacity and the ability to sustain activity; an immediate faster heartbeat is a response, not itself proof of improvement.

concreteCases.case: Manageable brief and repeated resistance tasks
concreteCases.reason: Relate suitable muscular work to force or continued effort; no maximal load or body-shape inference.
Relate range to easier movement in an activity; do not claim every stretch prevents injury or require a universal range.

concreteCases.case: An accessible familiar activity followed by a learning task
concreteCases.reason: Discuss attention/memory support as a possible benefit supported by child-specific public guidance; do not require that this particular child immediately feels happy or concentrates better.

protocols.task: Use the complete original four-component concept guide and its contrasting everyday cases, overlap/changed-purpose task and unsupported-inference diagnostic. Explain functional capacity and a relevant everyday benefit. This supplies G5 B2.2’s knowledge duty; its G6 links are conceptual components only.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Keep all four components and functional contrasts, strength versus repeated effort, justified overlap, changed-goal transfer and rejection of appearance/single-result inference. No personal performance norm is assessed by the knowledge task.

protocols.task: Use safe prepared actual activity with adult supervision and suitable individual access. Record ordinary responses before, during and after activity: perceived effort, breathing, warmth and, where appropriate and accessible, a gently found wrist pulse. Younger panels identify signs; later panels compare degree using an accessible simple method such as speaking comfort, breath sounds or perceived exertion. Explain relevant personal/context factors with a hypothetical comparison rather than private medical disclosure. Stop or adapt for discomfort; no deliberate heat, poor-air, cold or exhausted trial.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The Heart & Blood component retains the pump, continuous circulation, vessels reaching the body and appropriate heartbeat/pulse explanation. Feeling a pulse alone is not that full claim, and the full anatomy check does not by itself supply judging degree of exertion. Never enact injury/cut prompts. One elevated pulse is not lasting improvement or a diagnosis.

protocols.task: Create an actual repeated-observation portfolio under suitable adult supervision. Grade 5 chooses one component; Grade 6 considers all four. Use manageable comparable activity observations: a comfortable sustained route, brief suitable resistance action, repetition of a manageable action and comfortable joint motion as appropriate. Record the declared task/purpose, date, response and relevant support/context across occasions; compare with the person’s own earlier comparable evidence and state limitations. No maximum load, timed exhaustion, universal range, percentile or comparison of bodies is used.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The routine contribution retains actual tracking and reflection. The fitness concept supplies distinctions, not the observations. A blank template makes the source-fit assessment design available but does not claim a child has supplied the evidence. Changes in task or support must be acknowledged, not misread as measured adaptation.

protocols.task: Choose a realistic interest-based activity goal with a timeframe, identify steps, act on the plan on actual occasions, record progress and revise a step when necessary. Grade 2 also participates in a group goal with fair contributions; later panels use actual self-assessment and preferences to choose relevant fitness focus. Grade 5 chooses one component; Grade 6 uses assessment across the four-component model in planning. A plan written but never acted on does not fulfil implementation.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Retain the full goal-setting operation, including timeframe, steps, monitoring and adjustment. The routine panel includes the week record and a way to support another person; no forced disclosure or invented difficulty/frustration is needed. Hard-path mindset/mistake checks stay distinct rather than inferring a belief from goal completion.

protocols.task: In a prepared clear activity area, inspect a safe practice setup for a loose/defective equipment card, a blocked route and crowded movement space. Explain the risk and act appropriately: stop and report a fault, use an unobstructed route, keep safe personal space and follow actual directions/rules. Use only safe props and simulated hazards; do not scatter sharp objects or create a real trip. In an adult-supported demonstration, choose suitable protective equipment for the declared activity and check fit/condition without testing an impact. Equipment is not a guarantee against concussion.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Retain complete generic safety examples, trusted-adult knowledge and independent safe action. Rules require two reasons and a no-rule contrast, not only obedience; source-specific bodily/equipment control is actual behaviour, not inferred from reciting a rule.

protocols.task: Use declared original practice cases, not a current local forecast: a wet/slippery route; a hot sunny activity with accessible shade/water; a cold/windy case; and an AQHI practice value of 8 or above 10 with the actual Environment Canada health-message table. Identify the risk, interpret relevant warning information and choose preparation/adaptation, an indoor alternative or rescheduling with an adult. For the AQHI cases apply the child-specific category guidance; do not infer individual medical fitness. Grade 5 compares UV, heat/humidity, wind chill and air-quality information and explains proactive arrangements rather than waiting to become unwell. Actual sessions require the adult to check current local information and applicable school procedures. In a fictional medical-support case, check that a responsible adult has the learner-specific plan and prescribed support available; do not share/administer medicine, require private disclosure or test an allergy/asthma response.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Body-needs reasoning retains food, water, sleep and exercise as its separate whole check; hydration is a component, not the whole environmental duty. Signs use real Health Canada hazard-symbol pictures for a separate safe recognition check, plus actual school/local warning signs chosen by the adult. No chemical container is handled by a child.

protocols.task: Use the actual Ontario age-appropriate 2025 booklet: under-10 resource for the younger primary panel and ages 11–14 for the older panel. In fictional cases after an impact or not feeling right, stop the activity, promptly tell a responsible adult and ensure adult support instead of leaving a possibly injured child alone. Explain why an apparently normal appearance, no visible cut or no loss of consciousness does not clear return. Do not enact an impact, diagnose, move an injured person or practise symptom provocation. The adult uses the applicable school/local emergency procedure and obtains professional assessment as required. For Grade 6, bind a dated school/board concussion procedure before actual use, identify the responsible adults, and practise the learner’s reporting/removal/cooperation role. Ontario PPM158 supplies the verified provincial policy frame, not a claim that one invented school policy applies everywhere. Return clearance and graduated plans are adult/clinical responsibilities; no memorised recovery timetable or self-clearance.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Generic safety and rule claims contribute safe action, reasons and reporting; reading the booklet does not certify full brain/anatomy knowledge or clinical skill. Annual awareness/code confirmation is handled only where applicable to interschool sport, not invented as a new universal mastery score.

protocols.task: Use the complete approved minor-care guide and its three actual fictional case sets: adult-declared uncomplicated small scrape, adult-declared small bruise, then changed embedded-object/uncontrolled-bleeding/deep-wound/head-impact cases. Explain the different care methods and limits; no actual wounds, medication or physical treatment certification.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Retain the complete fixed concept: adult determines minor status; bleeding-control precedes cleaning/protection; wrapped cooling is comfortable and adult-timed; warning cases require prompt help without extraction or pressure on an embedded object.

protocols.task: Use the actual current Health Canada plate and recommendation bodies. Sort declared ingredients into vegetables/fruits, whole-grain and protein foods; use the plate proportions as a pattern reference, not a universal child portion or calorie prescription. Explain that food groups are not nutrients; use concrete food cases to distinguish energy, growth/repair and other body functions, including water. Construct a varied day pattern and adapt it to a supplied taste/cost/allergy/access constraint without declaring a culture or body good/bad. Keep the full existing nutrient inventory and day-menu check separate from any single source contribution.

Use neutral illustrated cases and the actual Food Guide hunger/mindful-eating bodies: an ordinary body cue, food being offered despite no noticed hunger, a changed activity/growth situation and comfort/fullness information. Recognise and explain how cues can inform choices alongside routine opportunities, access and adult medical advice. Voluntary ordinary noticing may use an accessible present sensation; never withhold food/water, manufacture hunger/fullness, require eating, ask about private intake/weight or score a child by appetite. Cues are one input, not an instruction to ignore a care plan or wait until thirsty before hydration.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Present-attention contribution retains deliberately selecting a focus, noticing an honest attention shift and returning in a changed context; no cue naming alone certifies it. Body Needs retains its entire food/water/sleep/exercise inventory; it alone does not teach every cue-guideline condition.

protocols.task: Use original supplied meal cases with declared ingredient and access information: a no-salt-added chickpea/vegetable curry with brown rice, a vegetable/whole-grain/protein lunch and an alternative when an adult-specified ingredient is unsuitable. Identify what the learner can choose and what an adult/environment controls. Check actual ingredient information and applicable adult medical support; no food challenge, medication or tasting is required. Compare at least two feasible options and consequences before choosing. Grade6 develops guidelines reflecting medical, emotional, practical and social factors rather than judging another household.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Food-hygiene contribution retains actual safe preparation/cleaning/storage/allergy checks separately, with adult oversight. Mere reading of a menu is not the full cooking-safety operation. Decision-making retains two options/consequences/reasoned choice, not only stating the right food.

protocols.task: Trace two declared cases, such as a grown chickpea made into a canned ingredient and a vegetable used fresh/frozen or in a prepared dish. Explain that ingredients and additions can alter nutrient content, while freezing/canning/drying can preserve food; not all processing is harmful. Use the actual Health Canada processing body rather than invented nutrient-retention percentages. Follow production, preparation, consumption and disposal; explain resource use and the difference between preventing edible-food waste and sending organic waste to landfill, using the actual ECCC body. No uncontrolled compost experiment, unsafe spoiled food or universal local/organic-is-better rule.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Food/fibre production contributes origin and process knowledge. Its complete cropping, grazing, horticulture, aquaculture, forestry/wool/cotton and attributed First Nations management checks remain broader separate assessments; one chickpea journey does not certify them or turn an Australian First Nations example into Canadian content. The explicit source task adds the nutrition/disposal connection; no full cooking-property or managed-environment claim is inferred.

protocols.task: Compare a declared water choice with frequent sugary-drink exposure and explain an oral-health implication using current Health Canada processing guidance, which explicitly links frequent sugary drinks with cavities in children. Explain why oral health matters and assess the choices, not just recite brushing. Retain the actual appropriate hand/tooth/cough hygiene whole-card tasks separately; no inspecting classmates mouths, inducing decay, body judgment or dental diagnosis.

Use the actual Health Canada food-guide version of Chickpea and vegetable curry and its brown-rice suggestion, together with the actual plate mixed-dish examples and a locally appropriate food card. Identify vegetable/protein/whole-grain contributions and explain how a different preparation can widen available healthy choices. Attribute this particular published version; curry is not one universal national or cultural recipe. No tasting, spice tolerance, ritual performance, private family identity or blanket claim about another community is required.

Plan a safe manageable eating-related routine using the actual Canadian guide, record it across a week, reflect on barriers and adjust a realistic interest-based goal. Later panels compare settings such as school/home/community and offer one feasible health-support action for another person without policing their body or diet. Record real evidence only at actual use; a provided template is not an invented learner history. Personal health details can remain private, with an adult-defined supplied case used for explanation.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Retain full routine week tracking/reflection/support and goal timeframe/steps/monitor/adjust. Do not infer a growth-mindset belief or manufacture frustration from completed diet-task steps. This is authored assessment design, not observed uptake.

protocols.task: Compare the actual government healthy-eating message with an explicitly original pretend food promotion: StarPower Crunch promises popularity with a celebrity-style character and a free token but provides no nutrient evidence. Identify commercial purpose and two influence techniques; check information rather than treat popularity as health proof. Reflect on an actual current response or safely chosen prior message without forcing a private purchase disclosure or claiming the child was influenced. For the inherited real-advertising prerequisite, inspect the actual LEGO10698 Canadian manufacturer advert: emotive creative-play language, product-variety/storage features and a shipping promotion. Use it as a real persuasion example, not an endorsement; no buying/signup/cart action. Separately use two original stated-price comparable-toy cases for value-for-money reasoning and retain the full needs/wants/money checks without asserting a universal history of barter.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Whole health-message interpretation retains inform/persuade/sell distinction, techniques and honest reflection. Whole Advertising & Spending has its own real-advert/two-technique/value/recalled-influence checks; a government warning alone does not supply that entire claim. No edge is weakened and a lack of recalled personal influence is insufficient evidence, not an invented deficit.

protocols.task: Combine a declared Canadian eating-pattern case with the qualified Active Living routine. Explain how both can support physical and mental/brain health, using the actually checked government bodies; one does not cancel unsafe choices in the other. Plan a feasible way to communicate or support both for others without weight/appearance targets, guarantees of mood or illness prevention, or requiring private diet/performance records.

Use the actual Canadian Nutrition Facts figure1 and ingredient/Contains image plus the actual current High-in explanation. Keep serving basis, ingredient/allergy information and nutrient-warning meaning distinct; no per 100 g Canadian column or overall Canadian star rating is invented. Separately use the original four two-column practice panels and given-rating case set. Locate per 100 g values for both cereals and both snacks, compare the specified nutrients on equal quantity, and justify a same-category choice using panel and rating together. The ratings are hypothetical givens in an explicitly Australian-context transfer, not algorithm-calculated commercial HSR scores. Whole-card success is not inferred from the Canadian task alone.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Keep all three unchanged whole evidence clauses, including both cereal sugar/fibre and snack sodium/saturated-fat per 100 g comparisons, and panel-plus-rating choice in a declared applicable context. Use given numerical quantities; no HSR calculation, caloric prescription or unit conversion is a mastery gate. Existing 11–12 contexts remain unchanged; the reviewed Grade 5 task supports the exact 10–11 component association.

protocols.task: Use an original school-pickup picture plan and fictional contact card: identify the agreed authorised adult and supervised waiting place, explain what to do if pickup changes, and demonstrate asking an appropriate adult for help. Rehearse an emergency call with an unconnected toy/screen using fictional details; distinguish an immediate emergency from a routine question. The adult binds the actual local pickup/contact procedure at delivery, privately. Older rows compare suitable trusted people and actual support-service functions for injury, distress, bullying, unsafe images and abuse; use the identified Kids Help Phone safe-adult information and an adult-prepared current school/community support card. Do not place a real call or submit a report as an assessment.
protocols.positive: Selects an appropriate person/service for the situation and communicates the needed help, with a changed pickup or unavailable-first-adult case.
protocols.nearMiss: Recites one number but cannot choose help, publishes private address/contact data, or assumes a familiar adult is always safe.
protocols.transfer: Change from school pickup to a fictional online threat or distressed friend; identify suitable safe adult/service and another option if the first does not help.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual local contacts and school routines are bound privately at use; no required personal disclosure, real emergency call or claim that a child is responsible for preventing adult abuse.

protocols.task: Use original non-graphic illustrated cases: a peer asks before borrowing a pencil; a child declines a hug; a carer explains necessary care; someone requests an unsafe secret or inappropriate touch. Identify caring versus harmful conduct, possible different feelings and an appropriate response. Explain who can give permission and that silence, freezing or pressure is not agreement; practise asking, waiting, respecting a refusal and choosing another option. Rehearse a clear boundary and a trusted-adult report using dolls or words, with no touch enactment. Include actual appropriate classroom permission alongside fictional unsafe cases.
protocols.positive: Connects respectful care to permission and boundaries, respects another person’s no and identifies help for harmful conduct.
protocols.nearMiss: Treats smiling, silence, friendship or prior permission as permission now, or blames a person who could not say no or leave.
protocols.transfer: Change from a possession to personal space and then a photo request; preserve the relevant person’s choice and adult safeguarding response.
protocols.sourceConditions: No actual sexual images, body inspection, simulated assault, unwanted touch, coercive role-play or private abuse history. Correct body-part/private-part knowledge remains a separate whole-card check using an ordinary labelled outline; no sensory tasting/nose-pinching from the inherited body-parts guide.

protocols.task: Use an adult-prepared actual school route/play area walkthrough and original home/community/online/outdoor picture cards. Identify a relevant hazard, explain a practical precaution and show the safe action where benign: stop at a marked pretend crossing, wait in the supervised area, ask before sharing food and leave a closed pictured chemical to an adult. Include a cold-storage/handwashing case and privately supplied care-plan responsibility where appropriate; no medication handling. Compare a safe online request with one asking for personal information or sending the learner away from an agreed site.
protocols.positive: Explains the risk and applies the relevant routine, not only names a hazard sign.
protocols.nearMiss: Gives one generic be careful answer across unlike hazards or demonstrates a dangerous exposure to prove understanding.
protocols.transfer: Change one location, weather condition or online request; adapt the precaution and identify when adult checking is necessary.
protocols.sourceConditions: Varied home/community/online/outdoor settings retained, examples not an exhaustive hazard inventory. Never use real chemicals, fire, traffic, railway tracks, unsafe water, animal approach, medical disclosure or unsupervised travel as a test.

protocols.task: Compare original family/caregiver/peer cards involving listening, cooperation and respectful disagreement with insult, deliberate exclusion and physical aggression. Describe possible feelings without requiring the target to show distress. Actually practise listening, an appropriate need/boundary statement and a benign shared-work compromise; use a fictional adult-harm case only to identify reporting and support, not to negotiate with the abusive person. Explain that anger can occur without making hurting someone acceptable.
protocols.positive: Distinguishes a feeling from a harmful action and demonstrates a constructive interaction while retaining adult safeguarding for abuse.
protocols.nearMiss: Treats crying or disagreement as wrongdoing, excuses violence as anger, or requires compromise with abuse.
protocols.transfer: Change a face-to-face disagreement into a fictional group-chat conflict and retain respectful communication and safe help.
protocols.sourceConditions: No forced smiling/calm feeling, apology or private family disclosure. Whole friendship and conflict-card evidence is checked separately from one kindness statement; actual safe listening/compromise is required where linked.

protocols.task: Read the actual Ontario Rowan’s Law under-10 booklet with a prepared adult: a concussion is a brain injury and can follow a hit to the head or a jolt to the body that moves the brain. Use original no-contact illustrated cases involving a fall or collision, including a case without obvious loss of consciousness. Explain why an adult must remove the participant safely and use the actual school-board process rather than letting the child diagnose or return because they feel better. Locate the relevant school reporting adult and supplied current return-to-learning/activity plan; no impact is enacted.
protocols.positive: Explains the injury/jolt relation and the reporting/removal/adult medical-authority boundary, not only wears a helmet.
protocols.nearMiss: Says all concussions require fainting, a helmet guarantees prevention, or a quick symptom check lets the child self-clear.
protocols.transfer: Change from a direct head impact to a body jolt; retain adult reporting and the school process without inventing a recovery timetable.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual G3 knowledge and how-it-occurs duty retained beyond a generic safety link. School protocol bound at use; no child diagnosis, medical clearance, deliberate impact, forced symptom recall or athletic return test.

protocols.task: In a supported group or individually, create and explain an original usable set of safety guidelines for at least three contrasting out-of-class settings, including online. Work from adult-checked local route, water/play and app mock-up information; identify the hazard, preventive action, reporting/contact and what would make the plan change. Walk through a benign mock scenario to check the guidelines and revise a missing step.
protocols.positive: Produces useful setting-specific guidelines with a reason and a changed-case revision.
protocols.nearMiss: Copies a generic poster with no application or treats the absence of a hazard in one photo as a universal guarantee.
protocols.transfer: Change a route closure, weather notice or unfamiliar online request and update the relevant step.
protocols.sourceConditions: The source requires developing guidelines, not only choosing a prepared rule. No real hazard trial; local adult approval is a delivery condition, not new child clinical authority.

protocols.task: Use an original two-panel cartoon in which a character is pushed, bounces up and continues unchanged; clearly label it invented fiction, not footage. Compare a non-graphic factual case card stating that a real push/fall can cause pain, injury and effects on the person and family that do not disappear at the end of a scene. Explain how another game/animation may omit or reverse those consequences and why the fictional reset is not evidence that real violence is harmless. Identify safe help rather than enact the push.
protocols.positive: Explains the mismatch between a particular fictional portrayal and possible real consequences, including effects on others.
protocols.nearMiss: Only says violence is bad, assumes every depiction is factual or claims every injury has the same outcome.
protocols.transfer: Change from a cartoon instant recovery to a game reset and explain the same representation limit.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual explanation across on/offline media retained; no violent clips, graphic injury images, enactment or deterministic medical claim. Actions-and-consequences contributes reasoning, not automatic topic-wide mastery from a single comparison.

protocols.task: Use an original mock game-chat and a fictional weekly screen/sleep/family timetable. Identify a privacy/contact risk and a time/relationship/sleep or comparison pressure; explain a practical precaution for each. Actually practise stopping a mock unsafe interaction, locating a report/block control with an adult and choosing an offline/help option. Discuss that risk is possible, not a diagnosis or a claim that all technology harms health. Review a changed request and a competing activity plan.
protocols.positive: Connects varied communication-technology risks to usable precautions and demonstrates the relevant mock action.
protocols.nearMiss: Only recites a password rule, diagnoses depression from time online or forwards/saves an unsafe image to prove the problem.
protocols.transfer: Change from a game contact to a photo request or bedtime message; retain privacy, support and a reasoned activity choice.
protocols.sourceConditions: No real accounts, stranger contact, image upload, naked/sexual images or private screen-history collection. Adult-bound local reporting route, no Australian service relabelled Canadian. Whole protective-action report/block checks remain explicit; advanced algorithm/AI ethics or financial scams are not assumed prerequisites.

protocols.task: Compare original non-graphic physical, verbal, exclusion and mean-message scenarios. Include repeated aggression with unequal power, a one-off serious harmful act and a mutual disagreement; explain possible impacts and safe responses without requiring the target to prove intention or wait for repetition. Use current Ontario guidance to distinguish conflict from bullying and recognise that all harm still warrants appropriate help. Rehearse an adult report and a safe bystander option; do not confront an aggressor or force mediation of abuse. For older rows include non-consensual image sharing by words/icons only, with no real image or screenshot.
protocols.positive: Identifies the conduct, power/permission concerns and suitable support/action, without minimising a single incident.
protocols.nearMiss: Says no help is needed until it happens twice, assumes calm appearance proves consent or requires the target to settle abuse by compromise.
protocols.transfer: Change the medium or relationship and retain the same safeguarding and non-blame principles.
protocols.sourceConditions: The inherited bullying card covers repeated-intended cases as a component; its narrower wording does not override current Ontario guidance or establish every one-off case is harmless. Keep old card/edges unchanged pending separate semantic review.

protocols.task: Actually work through original practical scenarios for preparing food, an accessible route and an online request: identify danger, generate at least two viable options, weigh likely consequences and adult-check needs, choose and act in a benign mock-up, then reflect and improve. Include one changed condition that makes the first plan unsuitable.
protocols.positive: Uses the process through action and reflection across different settings rather than lists its names.
protocols.nearMiss: Chooses an answer without alternatives/reasons, only discusses action or blames a person harmed despite precautions.
protocols.transfer: Change a resource or support and revise the plan with an explained consequence.
protocols.sourceConditions: No dangerous enactment or child guarantee of preventing harm. Whole decision/consequence checks retained; advanced quantified risk or cognitive-bias models are not imported.

protocols.task: Use clearly fictional non-graphic cards for an unsafe request, a threatening message and a person needing help. Prepare a short safe-response plan: notice relevant cues, choose a boundary/refusal or move-to-adult option, practise communicating the need and identify a fallback adult/service if the first is unavailable. Distinguish safe peer disagreement from coercion/abuse, which calls for adult protection rather than negotiated consent. Demonstrate on a neutral mock-up, not an ambush or fear test.
protocols.positive: Applies an appropriate safety/communication strategy and explains the next source of support in a changed situation.
protocols.nearMiss: Only looks confident, implies freezing makes harm the child’s fault or demands a distressed child perform a polished refusal.
protocols.transfer: Move from a fictional in-person request to online contact and adapt the response and support route.
protocols.sourceConditions: No manufactured fear, unsafe touch, personal disclosure or appearance/eye-contact/calm-mood criterion. A real inability to escape/refuse never removes the right to help.

protocols.task: Use original cases of a hurtful sexist/racist/homophobic comment, exclusion or unconsented image request, expressed only in age-appropriate description rather than slur reproduction or images. Explain how conduct may affect feelings, identity, well-being and reputation even if the speaker meant a joke. Propose and actually carry out a safe inclusive group-work action and listen to the other person’s preference; describe benefits to them and to oneself. In a benign real work-choice disagreement, express a need, listen, consider a compromise and check its effect; repeat in a mock online exchange.
protocols.positive: Connects intent versus impact, inclusion and actual constructive interaction, with a concrete changed action.
protocols.nearMiss: Only declares be kind, assumes smiling proves no harm or makes a targeted person responsible for forgiving or educating the group.
protocols.transfer: Change identity/context and medium; retain respect and an appropriate action without stereotyping everyone’s feelings.
protocols.sourceConditions: No private identity disclosure, compelled affiliation, slur rehearsal, public humiliation or forced positive feelings. Full prejudice/friendship/conflict/impact evidence remains separate where linked; no learner attainment inferred from a group product.

protocols.task: Use two original supported-care plans: an adult-supervised errand for a neighbour and preparing an agreed safe snack with a supplied fictional allergy plan. Identify what the learner can responsibly do, what needs an adult, relevant hazards and prevention, who to contact and the local emergency procedure. Compare a changed dangerous situation such as a fire alarm or possible reaction and explain stopping/obtaining adult help. Demonstrate benign steps only; the task does not certify independent babysitting, emergency treatment or unsupervised travel.
protocols.positive: Relates responsibility and risk to an appropriate preventive/responding plan, recognising limits of one’s role.
protocols.nearMiss: Lists risks without a usable procedure or attempts medicine, fire response or actual food exposure to demonstrate competence.
protocols.transfer: Change the cared-for person’s access need or the location/support and adapt the plan without assuming one rule fits all.
protocols.sourceConditions: Varied self/other-care duties retained; examples illustrative, not every medical emergency an extra topic. Individual/local procedures are adult-bound; actual help and fictional practice separated.

protocols.task: Use all three original case sets in ontario-hpe-allergy-claim-2026-11-11.json and the complete associated guide: varied known triggers, the same milk food linked to two supplied different conditions, and an unexplained possible reaction. Identify possible skin/breathing/digestive reactions without diagnosing from a symptom. Explain prompt prepared-adult help and supplied individual/emergency procedure, with no trial exposure or multiple-symptom threshold.
protocols.positive: Explains the bounded trigger/reaction model and its uncertainty in a changed fictional case.
protocols.nearMiss: Only checks whether food is clean, recites ask an adult without the knowledge, or diagnoses/tests a food from the case.
protocols.transfer: Change the named food and then remove the known clinical identity; retain appropriate uncertainty and adult help.
protocols.sourceConditions: Examples span several food families but are not an exhaustive allergy list. Fictional illustrations only; no exposure, private history, medicine, independent diagnosis or clinical triage.

protocols.task: Use an adult-prepared ordinary educational body outline and the actual external anatomy view from the attributed health resource, without any learner undressing or body comparison. Identify the main taught body parts and distinguish penis/testicles, vulva and vagina using correct respectful terms. Explain that bodies vary and that anatomical words name parts rather than insults or a person’s gender identity. Keep necessary-care/permission and trusted-adult-help checks separate under the existing whole body-autonomy claim.
protocols.positive: Correctly locates/names the taught parts with neutral language and distinguishes an external region from an internal canal.
protocols.nearMiss: Uses one vague word for every part, treats anatomical naming as permission to touch, or judges a person by appearance.
protocols.transfer: Change diagram orientation/skin tone and ask for the same structure without comparing actual bodies.
protocols.sourceConditions: Factual educational anatomy only; no body inspection, touch enactment, private sexual/medical history or demanded identity disclosure.

protocols.task: Use safe picture and real benign examples for all five senses: see a coloured shape, hear a comfortable quiet sound, feel a room-temperature texture with consent, describe familiar taste and smell examples without tasting/sniffing unknown material. Explain what each organ detects and that nerves carry information for the brain to interpret. Actually build/narrate a deliberate eye-to-brain-to-hand catch/point model and a changed hearing example for the complete existing brain-control check. Do not describe nasal hairs as the smell-message pathway or make every rapid withdrawal a conscious brain decision.
protocols.positive: Explains each sense’s functional contribution and the information/brain/response relation using an accurate changed example.
protocols.nearMiss: Only lists organs, assigns smell messages to hairs, or claims all sensory responses must wait for a conscious decision.
protocols.transfer: Change the starting sense and describe what information is detected and how an appropriate deliberate response follows.
protocols.sourceConditions: No blindfold/nose-pinching/food challenge, hot tray, loud sound or deprivation. Descriptive taste/smell cases are acceptable; old guide bytes/flags remain unchanged.

protocols.task: Actually demonstrate a full safe handwashing routine and a cough/sneeze-covering routine; explain when these reduce transmission and how personal items are safely handled. Use an ordinary toothbrush/floss demonstration model to show an appropriate brushing/flossing method and explain why regular dental advice matters. Privately choose an adult-supported personal-care routine without disclosing medical history or exposing the body; any real brushing/bathing occurs only in the ordinary private care setting, not as classroom inspection.
protocols.positive: Demonstrates the benign skills and connects them to health/transmission and oral care rather than naming products alone.
protocols.nearMiss: Recites wash hands while omitting important action, shares a toothbrush for a test or treats access to a dentist as a moral achievement.
protocols.transfer: Change from before-food to after-toilet/cough context and explain the relevant action; adapt the supported routine to a changed ordinary school day.
protocols.sourceConditions: No observed private washing, product insertion, genital handling, medical diagnosis or required purchase. Adult care advice/access remains a real delivery condition.

protocols.task: Order an original varied human life-course set from infancy through later adulthood and describe physical, thinking/feeling and social changes without presenting one family or ability pattern as universal. Explain how food/water/sleep/movement, safe surroundings and caring support can contribute to growth and living at different stages. Compare an infant needing care, a school child learning and a later adult with different possible supports; age does not determine worth or one fixed capability. Retain the existing animal-offspring/changed-young-to-adult example separately if that broader card is assessed.
protocols.positive: Orders the broad stages, describes relevant changes and gives reasons for varied physical/mental/social/environmental supports.
protocols.nearMiss: Only says people get taller, ends development at adulthood or assumes every older adult is helpless.
protocols.transfer: Change the fictional person’s access need or life stage and choose/explain a relevant support.
protocols.sourceConditions: No personal puberty deadline, family-history disclosure, ageing simulation or health deprivation. Animal-group inventory is a separate unchanged hard-chain assessment, not an extra HPE mandate.

protocols.task: Invite a low-stakes private or fictional reflection on what a body does, how it can be cared for and how respect can continue through change. Use original cases showing different abilities, skin/body features and access supports; compare a helpful care/support message with a stereotype or appearance-only judgement. Explain several factors affecting physical development, feelings/belonging and thoughts about the body. A learner can name frustration or dislike of a change while still identifying respect, care and support.
protocols.positive: Connects actual body functions/care with respectful responses and varied influences, without ranking appearance or forcing a positive feeling.
protocols.nearMiss: Says only one shape or ability deserves respect, equates body image with weight, or treats a smile as proof of acceptance.
protocols.transfer: Change the fictional stage, ability or social message and retain care/respect while acknowledging feelings can differ.
protocols.sourceConditions: Appreciation/comfort is contextual, not a binary forced-liking score. No body measurement, comparison, weight target or personal health disclosure.

protocols.task: Compare original caring/respectful friendship cases with exclusion, pressure or abusive conduct, identify the difference and explain an appropriate response. Actually practise asking/waiting/respecting a no in a benign possession or personal-space scenario. For older consent rows, explain freely given and changeable agreement, practise clear giving/refusing and stop/check for uncertainty; apply a reasoned decision in a changed photo/device/game scenario. Use fictional harm only to identify adult support, never to negotiate abuse.
protocols.positive: Explains healthy relationship features and actually demonstrates a respectful permission/consent and safe-response strategy.
protocols.nearMiss: Assumes friendship/silence means agreement or says the target is at fault for freezing or being unable to leave.
protocols.transfer: Change from a peer interaction to a mock online photo request and retain choice, privacy, support and changed-consent boundaries.
protocols.sourceConditions: No touch enactment, unsafe request ambush, sexual image, coercion, private relationship history or forced confidence/eye contact.

protocols.task: Use original fictional people with visible features and supplied less-visible preferences, beliefs, talents, learning/access needs or family experiences. Explain how neither appearance nor one label tells a whole identity, and choose/actually perform a safe respectful inclusion in ordinary group work. A person need not disclose an unseen characteristic for it to be respected.
protocols.positive: Distinguishes visible from not-readily-visible differences and connects respect to a concrete action.
protocols.nearMiss: Infers ability, beliefs, orientation or medical status from clothing/body features, or forces disclosure to justify inclusion.
protocols.transfer: Change which information is supplied and explain what remains unknown and how to act respectfully.
protocols.sourceConditions: No diagnosis or compelled cultural/medical/sexual identity disclosure. Differences are not a deficit ranking.

protocols.task: Use an original life-stage sequence and the current attributed health puberty resources to describe varied physical changes and possible emotional/social effects. For the complete existing puberty claim, order six or more stages, explain the broad uneven growth pattern and trace a simple gland-to-blood-to-change hormone-message model; do not introduce named feedback loops. Compare two same-age fictional people whose changes differ in timing. Discuss possible effects on friendships, privacy, independence, confidence and support without assuming everyone has a crush or feels the same way.
protocols.positive: Explains bodily changes, the broad hormone-trigger mechanism and varied possible social/emotional effects with a changed case.
protocols.nearMiss: Names hair/height alone, treats a fixed birthday as a deadline or attributes every feeling directly to one hormone.
protocols.transfer: Change stage/timing or a social situation and explain a reasonable care/support response without diagnosing.
protocols.sourceConditions: No actual development inspection, growth measurement, puberty-status disclosure or universal body timetable. Older whole reproduction knowledge is not inferred.

protocols.task: Explain how changing sweat/skin and ordinary daily activity can affect personal care, then make a feasible adult-supported private routine for washing, clean clothes, oral care and relevant individual equipment/access support. Actually demonstrate only benign public skills such as handwashing and model tooth cleaning; use clean unused product pictures/models for selecting suitable support, not personal application or inspection. Review an ordinary week privately and adjust a practical barrier with adult help.
protocols.positive: Links the changed needs to a usable routine and demonstrates appropriate benign hygiene rather than only buying a product.
protocols.nearMiss: Treats acne/body odour as proof of dirtiness or requires actual private washing to be observed.
protocols.transfer: Change the activity/access conditions and adapt the routine with a reason.
protocols.sourceConditions: No forced foreskin movement, internal cleaning, product insertion, medicine, body comparison or private-care surveillance; actual personalised advice stays with caregivers/clinicians.

protocols.task: Use the actual current OPH egg printed13/14 and sperm printed12 anatomy/process resources plus reproduction printed7–8. Hide labels, identify main structures and explain each function, including vulva/vagina and reproductive versus adjacent urinary/digestive organs. Trace egg release and variable uterine-lining shedding, and separately sperm production/maturation/transport with sperm distinguished from semen. Explain how the processes relate to possible fertilisation/implantation and development, while physical reproductive capability does not establish readiness for sex or parenting. Use changed view and scrambled process cards, not a personal body or cycle history.
protocols.positive: Actually explains both required source processes, structures/functions and their reproduction/development relation.
protocols.nearMiss: Only names external puberty changes, calls menstrual blood urine, places sperm production in the bladder or treats the example cycle as everyone’s fixed schedule.
protocols.transfer: Change diagram orientation and distinguish the no-pregnancy shedding route from gamete joining/implantation without a precise-day prediction.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual Grade5 reproductive structures/processes are independently assessed. The separate complete reproduction-whole-fit task accounts for the full existing tQk claim at the exact reviewed10–11 context, including gestation/birth/placental exchange and maternal effects; no inference from a puberty-only answer.

protocols.task: Use a fictional identity map showing qualities, people, places, culture, abilities, body-image messages, support and orientation as intersecting aspects of a person’s self-concept. Define orientation factually without assigning it from anatomy, appearance or stereotypes, and distinguish it from gender identity/expression where useful using the actual public-health FAQ. Explain how inclusion, supportive relationships and challenging stereotypes can support well-being; they do not cause or choose someone’s orientation. For the existing identity whole-card check, a learner may privately use ordinary likes/strengths/groups/place examples without disclosing protected identity or distress.
protocols.positive: Explains interacting influences on self-concept and a practical support/response without deterministic claims or disclosure demands.
protocols.nearMiss: Treats family/media as a simple cause of orientation, assumes anatomy identifies gender/orientation or requires a learner to label themselves.
protocols.transfer: Change a fictional person’s support or stereotype context and explain a constructive response while preserving what is unknown.
protocols.sourceConditions: No identity test, coming-out task, belief compliance, private orientation disclosure or fixed national cultural model.

protocols.task: Use three original fictional cases: an ordinary question about a body change, a disagreement about new independence and persistent distress interfering with daily life. Describe possible emotional/interpersonal stresses and distinguish a need for professional adult support from diagnosing by one mood. Choose an appropriate coping strategy, rehearse asking a trusted adult and plan/rehearse a benign upcoming transition; after an ordinary real change reflect privately on what helped. Include access to accurate information and a fallback helper, without promising one strategy cures a mental-health condition.
protocols.positive: Recognises a concerning pattern as a reason to seek help, chooses a contextual strategy and actually rehearses communication/transition support.
protocols.nearMiss: Diagnoses a condition from one sad moment, claims everyone must be happy about puberty or treats coping as a substitute for necessary professional care.
protocols.transfer: Change the stressor or first support’s availability and adapt the response with a reason.
protocols.sourceConditions: No induced distress, private symptom score, medical diagnosis, forced sharing or treatment prescription. Whole coping/check-after-change evidence remains separate from a fictional safe-help answer.

protocols.task: Use three original non-graphic statement cards about fictional staged sexual media: a portrayal omits asking or checking consent; bodies are edited/presented in one narrow way; a scripted interaction is offered as a guide to caring relationships. No image, sexual-act description, video or website is shown or sought. Explain how such portrayals can give a limited/unrealistic account of bodies, gender expectations and relationships, and compare them with respectful communication/consent and varied real people. State that effects can vary and that accidental exposure is not the child’s fault; a trusted adult can help.
protocols.positive: Explains a concrete possible representation/expectation mismatch and an appropriate respectful alternative, not merely labels media bad.
protocols.nearMiss: Treats a staged depiction as proof of real consent/body norms or shames a child who encountered material.
protocols.transfer: Change the misleading claim and explain its limit without viewing actual material or assuming everyone is affected identically.
protocols.sourceConditions: The source’s explicit-media knowledge duty is retained with a non-explicit discussion design; general stereotype knowledge alone does not establish it. No pornography access/search, real image, disclosure, diagnosis or universal causal claim.

protocols.task: Use original non-slur fictional examples about gender expectations, orientation, race/culture, mental health and abilities. Explain possible effects on self-concept, inclusion and relationships, distinguish an individual from a group assumption and propose a specific response. Actually practise a safe inclusion or correcting-question response in ordinary group work, without making a targeted learner educate the group.
protocols.positive: Connects a particular assumption to possible harms and a reasoned constructive change across varied contexts.
protocols.nearMiss: Only says be nice, repeats a slur, treats a stereotype as fact or asks a peer to disclose identity to disprove it.
protocols.transfer: Change the group/context and explain what carries over and what needs checking rather than replacing one stereotype with another.
protocols.sourceConditions: No compulsory positive feeling, private identity disclosure, public humiliation or universal response claimed for a community.

protocols.task: First use the OPH Grade5 diagrams and process tasks, then hide labels. Identify both systems’ structures and explain functions in own words. Explain sperm and egg roles and where/what fertilisation is. Arrange and explain the complete development/birth sequence. Build and explain the placental exchange model, rejecting blood-mixing and stomach-growth alternatives. Apply the supplied maternal-effect fact to the same model. Separately explain menstruation when no pregnancy occurs and sperm production beginning at puberty, their relation to reproduction and normal variation. Spoken, pointed, drawn or written explanations are allowed; naming alone does not replace causal explanation.
protocols.positive: Coordinates structures/functions, gamete joining in the oviduct, implantation and growth in uterus, birth and two-way exchange across separate blood supplies; uses the maternal-effect case coherently and retains the actual Grade5 menstrual/sperm-production duties.
nearMiss: Correct external puberty-change list but no reproductive process explanation.
Places fertilisation in the bladder or growth in the stomach.
Calls sperm and egg merely touching rather than joining.
Shows maternal blood flowing directly into the foetus or treats placenta as a food store only.
Says a separate blood supply blocks every harmful substance.
Repeats arrows but cannot explain a reversed waste arrow or a changed diagram.
protocols.transfer: Use a differently oriented unlabelled diagram and an unsequenced set with one deliberate error: fertilisation in uterus, baby in stomach, or waste travelling towards baby. Correct and explain it. Then explain why a harmful substance can cross although whole blood supplies normally do not mix. Contrast lining shedding without implantation against the pregnancy sequence; no fixed monthly timetable for every person.
protocols.sourceConditions: The supplemental placental/birth/maternal-effect task is a whole-claim fit check, not an extra universal Ontario requirement. Passing only the Grade5 source task never certifies the whole tQk claim, and passing a hypothetical authoring rubric is not any learner observation.

At birth the uterus contracts and the baby leaves the uterus; in a vaginal birth the cervix opens and the baby passes through the vagina.
originalAssessmentMaterials.sequenceAnswer: Use this order for the supplied fertilisation-to-vaginal-birth model; explain growth over months, not an exact due-date calculation. Birth can also occur by an operation performed by medical staff; that is not a failed or abnormal family history and is not a clinical-procedure gate.
